title: Writing the methods section
outcome: Explain writing the methods section using the records and boundaries of this fictional investigation.
scenario: Methods that another team can repeat. A paper describes a toy string-classification experiment using a stated length rule.
given: Inputs: "oak", "pine", "willow". Rule: length at least 4→long, otherwise short. No whitespace trimming occurs.

steps.label: Record exact inputs
steps.detail: Preserve the three strings and no-trimming policy.

steps.label: State procedure
steps.detail: Apply the inclusive length boundary at four characters.

steps.label: Show resulting labels
steps.detail: Oak is short; pine and willow are long.

explanation: A methods section specifies inputs, processing, boundaries, versions and scoring. Precise procedures allow a reader to repeat the computation instead of inferring it from the final labels.

counterfactual.change: Change the rule to length greater than 4.
counterfactual.prediction: Pine becomes short; willow stays long and oak stays short.
counterfactual.reason: The equality case distinguishes the two procedures.

student_task: Apply the inclusive four-character rule to oak, pine and willow. Which label changes under greater-than-four, and what method detail allows another team to reproduce the distinction?
teacher_answer: Preserve the three strings and no-trimming policy. Apply the inclusive length boundary at four characters. Oak is short; pine and willow are long. Changed case: Pine becomes short; willow stays long and oak stays short. The equality case distinguishes the two procedures.
project_evidence: For the Reproducible AI Research Study, retain an annotated worked trace and the changed-case reasoning. Connect the claim to its records, units and assumptions so another investigator can challenge or reproduce it.
limits: Repeating this deterministic toy rule does not validate a learned model or establish ecological categories.
review_note: Individually authored fictional practice distinct from the reserved independent case. No invented significance, real experiment execution or pupil outcome is asserted.
